precepts.label: Proverbs 15:10
precepts.why:
Cain was born first, just like Esau. “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground”, a man of the field, which already tells you what is going on. “And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” Cain already knew right from wrong, because his father taught him animal sacrifice, but over a process of time Cain turned evil and did not do what the Lord commanded.

Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:” “But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” His countenance fell because he was corrected. What really started all of this? Correction.

Solomon says, “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way”. Cain had forsaken the way over a process of time, so the correction was grievous to him. That grievous spirit nourished bitterness, and the bitterness grew until he murdered his brother. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with a bitter spirit.

Then: “and he that hateth reproof shall die”, because the wages of sin is death. Paul says, “For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.” If we judged ourselves we would not have to be told about the bitterness, envy, hatred and malice inside us; when we refuse, the Lord has to bring the chastening. Cain refused to get himself right, and he became the father of wickedness.

precepts.label: Proverbs 13:10
precepts.why:
Bitterness does not travel alone. Envy, pride, hatred and evil suspicion come bundled together like a cable TV package. Solomon names one: “Only by pride cometh contention”.

Cain was contending because pride was on him. Cain's attitude was: I am not going to make it right with my brother; my brother is the one who is off; in fact, I have to put him to death, because he is making me look bad. That is pride. Cain did not want to take the correction.

Then: “but with the well advised is wisdom.” The well advised are the ones who do well, like Abel. Wisdom says, let me get my spirit right; I cannot have an evil eye toward my brother. When correction comes, pride contends with it, while wisdom takes it and makes things right with the brother.

precepts.label: James 3:16
precepts.why:
“For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” Genesis 4 is an account of envying and strife. Cain was not doing right, he saw Abel doing right, and that built envy, the same spirit that shows up later between Esau and Jacob. It was there from the beginning.

Then comes confusion. All of a sudden Cain did not know right from wrong, and every evil work followed: he slew his brother. When you are confused, saying, I do not know where this is coming from, every evil work will be the result.

Confusion is Satan's playground. Satan loves us operating in confusion. That is why his children throw every kind of confusion into the media and everywhere they go, and why leaders of other nations have said they do not want that American media in their countries. They know every evil work hides behind that cloud of confusion.

precepts.label: Galatians 5:26
precepts.why:
“Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.” Cain wanted to be the man; that is vain glory.

Provoking one another means agitating a brother to play him out of position, because you are envious of him. You do something to provoke him to evil so you can justify your position against him.

We see this even in marriage. A brother provokes his wife, she leaves the house and does something foolish, and he sits back saying, I told you the sister was off, I told you she was evil. No, brother: you are the evil one, you provoked your wife. We are not going for that foolishness here. Envy provokes, and provoking is how the bitter spirit sets up its victim.

precepts.label: Romans 7:11
precepts.why:
What is bitterness? It is sin. “For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.” Taking occasion by the commandment means you can only recognize sin through the commandments of God. How do you know you are in the middle of sin? The law says you shall not hate your brother in your heart, and when you meditate on it you realize, I have an evil spirit toward that brother. The law brings it to the surface.

Sin “deceived me”: you did not know bitterness was a sin, because you were deceived. But the law gives clarity. Like fog lights, it pierces the cloud of confusion. That is why the law is called a light: so you can see through the nonsense your mind was thinking.

Then sin “by it slew me.” When the scripture comes out, you feel cut, because you are no longer deceived and can see clearly. What you see on the other side of the fog is yourself in the mirror of the Bible, realizing how evil you were. Some people do not like the light and love to walk in darkness, saying, do not call that out, that is not me; brothers wearing purple and gold, a ribbon of blue and fringes, who are only blue ribbon Christians. We do not want to be those night walkers.

precepts.label: Psalms 37:8
precepts.why:
“Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.” That bitterness is the spirit of Cain, and in that wrath you might slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray one. None of us is above this. Do not sit in the congregation thinking so-and-so is getting cut with the scriptures; brother, that is you. Every lesson the leadership brings out is for us. The moment you think, I am not dealing with that, Satan already has you lined up and counts you on his team.

Go back to Genesis 4:8: “And Cain talked with Abel his brother”. This is the deception. Cain acted like his friend, talking with him over time about his flocks, until he could lure him out to the field: “when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” Solomon describes that man: “He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;” “When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.” Murder, envy, pride and covetousness are all in there. “Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.” That is why it is called a root of bitterness: roots are covered by soil where nobody can see them, but the Lord always brings it to the surface. “Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein”, and “a flattering mouth worketh ruin.”

John names the spirit: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was the first recorded hater in the scriptures, and he came back as Esau. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead; carry an evil eye toward your brother and you are in the same spirit. “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death.” “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer”. And Sirach warns, “When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” Brothers say, the white man is the devil, they are going to be destroyed, they are going into captivity, and then carry hatred toward their own brother, moving in the same spirit.

“Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.” Bitterness is a progression: it starts with a correction or an offense, then pride comes in and you will not speak to the brother, then when you do speak it is in deceit, masking envy, anger and hatred, and in the end it destroys you and those around you. “A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump”: a little bitterness defiles the whole soul. Christ said, “Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.” “For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed”. Leaven looks flat at first and grows as it bakes, so do not let the hate bake. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God before it festers and overcomes you.

precepts.label: Genesis 33:4
precepts.why:
“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” That is the bitterness, and it plans over a process of time. It is the same thing we read in Genesis 4: Cain slew Abel, and Esau wanted to kill Jacob. Cain was the firstborn and Esau was the firstborn. Same spirit.

To see how someone can hold bitterness, hatred and malice toward you and hide it completely, look at Genesis 33, long after Esau said he hated his brother: “And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.” Someone who hates you can play the long game. He can pretend to be your friend and on your side while he waits for the moment to hit you at your worst. They call them liberals today. That's the liberal for you: oh, we love you niggers, I mean black people. Jacob knew Esau's heart. That is why he sent the gifts ahead: he thought Esau might be coming to kill him.

Hebrews explains what was working in Esau: “Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled”. Looking diligently means looking within yourself. The root of bitterness is a hidden sin under the ground that nobody sees, but over time it springs up and troubles you. It distorts your thoughts and your perception, so that things you once saw clearly, with eyes anointed with eye salve, are no longer pure to you.

“Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” Profane means devoted to what is not sacred, secular rather than religious: Esau was a carnal man, a man of the field, whose religion is sin. When we follow the carnal ways of Esau, we throw away our birthright, the kingdom of heaven. Hebrews says “for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.” Hold on to a bitter spirit and you are a spiritual Edomite, and you will find the same place of no repentance on that day.

An officer drew the parallel: “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” Christ came “that he might destroy the works of the devil”, so we cannot move in the devil's spirit and think we move in Christ's. Whoever does not love his brother is not of God. If there is an offense, deal with it by Matthew 18:15, not by sowing discord in the congregation. “For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” The spiritually minded man seeks to gain his brother, not keep him as a rival to get back at, “Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God”.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:19-20
precepts.why:
Esau cried, “Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing.” Is that true? Go back to Genesis 25. Esau came from the field faint and said, “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”. “And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.” There was no trickery. Jacob asked him straight, and it was up to Esau to say no. Esau said, “what profit shall this birthright do to me?” Jacob made him swear, because the word of that man is no good, just as with the four hundred and some treaties they broke. Scripture sums it up: “thus Esau despised his birthright.”

So Esau was lying and playing the victim. The Psalm describes it: “Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit.” “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Did we not just read the slander? He tricked me two times. Nowhere does scripture show Jacob dealing with deceit over the birthright. They were liars from the beginning, because they moved in the same spirit as their father Cain, who was of the wicked one.

It is how they do today: throw the rock, hide the hand, and as soon as the other side hits back, run to the UN as the victim. Now all of a sudden he cares about the birthright, just as his children want to stand in our place claiming to be the Jews and the people of the book. Where was that energy when he threw it away for something to eat, or today for money and fame?

You got the children of God and you got the children of the devil; there is no in between. You either got the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The same Psalm says to the wicked, the white man, “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” “Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” They say in God we trust and swear on the Bible while doing nothing the scripture says.

Esau “lifted up his voice, and wept”, but that was worldly sorrow. “For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.” We must come to the Lord sincerely, because of those who wait, God says, “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:” “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. “Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way”. We all have to examine ourselves so we are not moving in that same spirit.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 3:16-17
precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses”. That is purging the old leaven. We had to do it physically, but it is something spiritual today. So what is your house today? “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” You, me, we are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God is to dwell in us because our temple was destroyed.

Look at how we purge leaven from the house. Brothers dump out the toaster, sweep underneath the floor mats and in the corners where stuff builds up. There is not one grain of yeast in the house. Meanwhile the brother has an evil eye toward another brother, or is bitter toward his wife, or vice versa. We sweep our houses with diligence; we must do the same with our spirit, because we are the temple of God.

“If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” You will pull this out on a brother in the street: brother, you got tattoos, you got the devil on you, you are defiling your temple. We know tattoos are wrong. But meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If you are out there with the leaven of bitterness in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if he and you do not repent.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.” What is that really saying? How do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps into your mind and you say, damn, I don't like that brother. You are spiritually consuming it, entertaining sin and not purging the leaven from your house. That is how you get cut off from your people, and this is a serious thing.

How you get cut off: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Christ is our Passover, who set the example. That is the gift, the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins, because we are in a wicked place.

And Exodus 13:7 says “there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.” We do not want to be seen in the midst of sin, Passover or not. Don't be the brother who does not throw the bread out but puts it in his storage closet and brings it back when Passover is over: laying the bitterness aside for the season and picking right back up hating the brother. That is not the spirit. Throw it out. Let it go.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20
precepts.why:
Some brothers say, I am going to tuck mine in, tuck away my hatred and my bitterness and save it for later. Paul answers that: “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?”

We are not our own. So when we hide hatred, bitterness, malice, whatever sins we deal with, we are throwing that back in Christ's face. He is our Passover, our sacrifice; he bought us back, twice he bought us back. So we do not own our bodies to even have the angle to defile our temple. When a brother lends you something, you are supposed to take extra care of it. Christ gave us our bodies and bought us back again, and we need to keep them like brand new.

“For ye are bought with a price”: with Christ's blood. Then, “therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” We have to use our bodies to glorify him in every way possible, and our spirit too, because both belong to God. When we hold back malice, hatred for our brothers or hatred for our wife, we put that on Christ, and it is not of the Lord. We have to let go of that spirit.

That is the leaven Exodus 12:15 says to put out of your house: not only the yeast on the box, but the bitterness tucked in when Bishop comes around and let out again when he leaves.

precepts.label: Numbers 14:27-34
precepts.why:
Exodus 13:8 says “And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.” This is done means the feast of unleavened bread. But what did the Lord do unto me? The Lord delivered everyone, but did everyone enter the promised land? No. Numbers 14 shows what he did.

“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me?” When we came out of Egypt, our people were evil. You thought they were righteous? They were rebellious: a bunch of liars, fornicators, murmurers. The Lord said, “as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward”. Once you were twenty years old and up, the Lord said, all of you are going to die. Aaron died. Moses died too; not that Moses was evil, but the people provoked him to anger, so he did not see the promised land, though when he left his body he was going back to paradise.

“Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.” Joshua and Caleb were the only two adults the Lord allowed to make it in. According to the law, at twenty you are the age of a man and take responsibility for yourself, which is why twenty is the age to marry. Everybody twenty and up, their blood was on their own head.

“But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.” The children wandered forty years and bore the whoredoms of the adults, seeing all the evil they did, “until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness”: until every last one of those wicked Israelites died, everybody who had leaven in them, the murmurers, the adulterers, the ones who held on to Egypt.

So the me of Exodus 13:8 is not Moses. It is the little ones, twenty years and under, who grew up in the land and told their sons: we keep unleavened bread because the Lord purged the leaven out of me in the wilderness. And it is the same in the future: whoever keeps leaven, which is sin, through the seven days, that soul shall be cut off.

precepts.label: Isaiah 58:9
precepts.why:
Samuel asked Saul, “Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the Lord?” King Saul had an issue with being obedient to the Lord, and God called that disobedience evil in his sight. Saul answered, “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord”, and then, “But the people took of the spoil.” Was that a sign of godly sorrow? No, there was none involved. Isaiah 58:9 names what Saul was doing.

“Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity.”

What is the putting forth of the finger? That is blaming. Saul blamed the people right after saying he had kept Agag alive. He blamed the people for keeping the sheep and the best of the flocks, but did not take accountability for keeping Agag the Amalekite alive. So what does the Lord say? He is not going to hear any of us until we stop playing the blame game. The Lord answers, “Here I am”, when the finger is taken away.

Stop blaming others. How are you dealing with that situation? I am bitter against this person because they did this to me; I have hatred towards this person because of this. The Lord does not care about your reasoning or your justification, because every one of us will be judged according to our ways. The Lord sees how that person is treating you, and the same way he sees how you are reacting to that treatment. If you trust in the Lord, you act according to how God commanded you to deal with that situation, and then let the Lord deal with that person.

That is a building block of bitterness. Disobedience, then justifying yourself, then blaming others: the bitterness is compounded on sins that were already there. As 1 Samuel 15:22 says, “to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.”

thread.label: Proverbs 16:6
thread.text: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.

precepts.label: John 15:1-5
precepts.why:
“By mercy and truth iniquity is purged.” Going into Passover season, which is also purging season, we refocus and get rid of the spiritual leaven known as sin. Christ shows how the purging is done: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.”

A vine is nothing more than a root sprouting through the ground, and Christ is that root: “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” And the Father is the husbandman because we are what he planted: “ye are God’s husbandry, ye are God’s building.” We are his plants, his trees, which in that day become the trees of righteousness.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” That is why we cannot be like the brother who had the talent and hid it. If we do not bring forth fruit, he takes away our candlestick: you did not do what I created you to do, so you cannot be here. One bad apple spoils the bunch, and you are going to hinder growth, so you have to be taken out of the way.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” That is the purging of Proverbs 16:6: iniquity purged, so we keep growing in the spirit and getting closer to our Lord and our God.

“Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.” We have to stay steadfast and abide in Christ: not loving our pleasures or our lust more than Christ, but doing the will of the Father and his Son.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:19-21
precepts.why:
“Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” The Lord already knows who are his; we do not, but God does. And God also establishes leaders to guide you along the way, so that you do not fall into the wiles of Satan or stumble into pitfalls and never recover.

“And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” That is purging from sin, from the spiritual leaven, the same as “by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.”

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is Israel. Just as not all the crops take root, in the house of Israel you have the good ones and the bad ones, some to honour and some to dishonour.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: not from the gold and silver, but from the wood and the earth. Those who are not producing fruit, those with dead spirits, those always caught up in some mess, those who separate from the leaders the Lord established. How did you learn what the new moon was? You saw a video of our leadership teaching it. But then you come in here and do not want to be around them; you want to be with the clique in the back. That is the wood and the earth, and God is telling you to purge yourself from those people if you want to remain steadfast in Christ.

Then “he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” God can use you.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:4-9
precepts.why:
“Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.” That escape from corruption is the purging of iniquity in Proverbs 16:6, and it has to be kept up.

“And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue.” We have to be diligent. We cannot just come in here knowing that Christ is black, God is black and the angels are black. When we come through these doors we have to add to our repertoire, add to our spirit: “virtue; and to virtue knowledge; And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.”

“For if these things be in you, and abound”: not just be in you, but be in you and grow. “they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Meaning you do not have to be purged out. If you can do that, you do not have to worry about being taken out of the mix, because you are constantly growing and doing the Lord’s will.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind.” Sin has blinded you. You cannot think straight, you cannot do what is common sense, you struggle constantly and never break through, because you have not purged yourself from the wrong people and you love that pleasure more than God. He “cannot see afar off”: you cannot see that America is going to be destroyed and that salvation is coming. You are a situational Israelite living in the moment, thinking America is going to last forever. Shame.

He “hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” God purged you from your old sins, but if you do not keep trimming, if you do not keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly. This is a wake-up call, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness.

classes.title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.label: 1 John 1:9
precepts.why:
“He that covereth his sins shall not prosper”: when you try to cover that bitterness, the roots keep growing, and you are just bringing in dump trucks to load more soil on top of it. But whoso confesses shall have mercy, and John shows why: “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins”. The Lord is faithful and just when we confess our sins.

That goes all the way back to Leviticus. When you brought your sacrifice before the priest, that was a public confession. You had to walk through the midst of all Israel with your offering.

Now we have the white man, his walls and his technology. We have VPNs: yeah, don't nobody know I'm on OnlyFans, I got a VPN, I'm broadcasting from the Philippines. No, brother, the Lord sees right through it.

So in order to get over the root of bitterness we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. Covering it will never prosper; confessing it is how we get the mercy we all want.

precepts.label: James 5:16
precepts.why:
Confessing is not only to the Lord. James says: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.”

We should be comfortable confessing our faults, because, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 says, no temptation has taken you but such as is common to man. You confess your fault, and a brother might say, brother, I was dealing with the same spirit. Woo, man, I feel a lot better. All of this is common. We all have levels of bitterness; some have a higher degree than others, but everybody deals with a level of bitterness, a level of lust, a level of lack of faith.

That doesn't mean getting on the public announcement. It means you see a godly man and say, hey Cap, hey D, I have this going on, I need help with it. They are going to help you. They are not going to say, brother, you got the devil on you, get away from me. It is Satan telling us otherwise.

That is whoso confesseth and forsaketh: confessing to the Lord, confessing one to another, and being healed, instead of covering the sin and letting the root grow.

thread.label: Proverbs 29:20
thread.text: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.

precepts.label: Sirach 7:36
precepts.why:
“Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.” A hasty man acts off of impulse, and the answer to that is not to act off of impulse but to think it through: “Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss.”

Whatever we take in hand, we remember the end. We have to be in that frame of mind, and we have to be around the right people, being around the righteous and staying occupied in the work. Whoever commits sin while being around the righteous family, Satan is heavy on him.

So when we are tempted, we can think things through and remember the judgment of the Lord, and the fear activates, and then we can overcome.

That is the whole choice set out in Romans 6: “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” Fall into sin and in that moment you are serving the devil, because you cannot have two masters. Remembering the end is how a hasty man learns patience, resolve and discipline.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:15
precepts.why:
“Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God.” We have to be diligent, constantly abounding in the work, because if we are not, we can fall from the grace of God.

“lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you.” If you are not occupied in doing the Lord’s work, not putting your hands to the plow, not studying, not being amongst the righteous, a root of bitterness can spring up in you, because you are not studying to combat it. You might have a feeling, but you had better rebuke that thing, and the way to do it is to be around these people.

If you draw back and separate from your people, Satan has you right where he wants you. Now he can play on your psyche and your mind. When you are not constantly seeing people you start thinking differently: they never liked you anyway. That is what Satan does.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” Satan wants to devour all of us, just as Christ told Peter that Satan desired to have him to sift him as wheat. We have to be in that mindset and know what is going on. The hasty man who does not look diligently lets bitterness spring up, and he is worse off than a fool.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:17
precepts.why:
“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” When you hear a class like this, do not say, Oh, that ain’t it. You are just making an excuse to go back to your pleasure and your lust, to feel comfortable in them.

The excuse maker starts a fight over the chicken so he can leave and get some duck. It is like the story the Bishop told about the co-worker who dealt with multiple women and would start a fight with one to go see the other. Now you are pointing the finger at everybody else, when back at the ranch you really want to go have fun in your pleasure and your lust. As the Bishop’s graphic says, a sin-filled soul will find and make excuses only to fulfill its lust. That is very dangerous.

“A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies.” And “Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.”

So we have to have fear and we have to be diligent if we want a fighting chance. The man hasty in his words, who always has an excuse ready, will not be reproved, and that is why there is more hope of a fool than of him.

precepts.label: Sirach 23:2
precepts.why:
The hasty man needs control, and control comes by discipline: “Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins.” We have to learn discipline so we do not end up looking crazy out here.

“For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love.” The very true beginning of following after wisdom is the desire of discipline. So we have to fight temptation, fight off the devil and overcome the beast in order to learn that discipline.

“Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” We have to put on all of the armour. If you are not studying, you are not battling; you are just falling victim.

Keeping God’s commandments does not give instant gratification. The consequences are delayed: we are going to get the kingdom. Sin gives you the pleasure right then and there, the instant dopamine, and once you are hardened by the deceitfulness of sin you no longer see any reason to keep God’s commandments because they do nothing for you in the moment. In this truth you have to self-motivate. You cannot wait for somebody else to give you a pep talk. You have to discipline your own soul if you want to make it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:50
precepts.why:
“So shall righteousness hate iniquity, when she decketh herself, and shall accuse her to her face, when he cometh that shall defend him that diligently searcheth out every sin upon earth.” We have to learn to hate iniquity. We have to discipline our minds to hate iniquity and to hate sin. If we want the Lord to defend us, that is what we have to do.

Wisdom of Solomon shows the end of both sides. The ungodly say, “Even so we in like manner, as soon as we were born, began to draw to our end, and had no sign of virtue to shew; but were consumed in our own wickedness.” The hope of the ungodly “is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.”

“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.” You may not see it right now, but if you keep God’s commandments, if you do the homework, you are going to live forever, while everything that feels good in the moment passes away. The Most High cares for you, if you are able to hate sin.

That is the answer to the hasty man: discipline the mind to hate iniquity, and the Lord defends the one who diligently searches out every sin.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:27
precepts.why:
The first sign of a bitter brother is that he is easily offended; he will “make a man an offender for a word”. The next sign is that he holds grudges, the thing Leviticus 19:18 forbids: “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people”. And he is always revisiting past wrongs.

Proverbs names him: “An ungodly man diggeth up evil”. That is the bitter brother digging up evil, the plumber brother, digging up old ish. As we say up in the States, he's digging it up like he's a plumber.

“and in his lips there is as a burning fire.” That is deceit, and he is always hating. That is the brother with the banana on his lips, the certified hater like Cain: I don't like that. That's you.

So the one who makes a man an offender for a word is the same one who keeps digging up the old things. He lacks forgiveness, as Sirach 28 showed, and he will not let the past rest. Brother, you are not in the right spirit.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 20:22
precepts.why:
Another sign of bitterness is quiet resentment: they sit back and stew in silence. Sirach shows that brother: “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness”. He is the bitter bashful brother, brother BB.

“and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.” He'll say, man, brother, everything good. Then he is told, brother, I need you to go do this, this and this, and he says, yes sir. The whole time he is thinking, I ain't feel like doing ish for that MF. He says yes sir to your face, and he has no intention in his heart of doing it.

That is the same bitter spirit as the one that makes a man an offender for a word, only hidden. The loud one digs up evil; the bashful one smiles and resents in silence. Either way he destroys his own soul, and he overthrows himself.

thread.label: Isaiah 35:1-10
thread.text: The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.

precepts.label: Revelation 5:12-13
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the wilderness and the desert shall be glad and “blossom as the rose.” When we are delivered, the desert places in our land will blossom and trees will start springing up, because we are connected to the earth. When the righteous people start ruling, everything changes. The animals are free, and the creatures understand us. That may sound like church talk, but the donkey did talk to Balaam: why are you beating me? Revelation shows how far that understanding goes.

“Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.” Christ receives all these things.

“And every creature which is in heaven”: those are the angels. There are creatures in heaven. “and on the earth”: the animals created on the earth. “and under the earth”: creatures created in the earth, worms and such, and creatures living deep in the earth that nobody has ever seen. “and such as are in the sea”: leviathan, and creatures in the sea no human being has ever seen, that the Lord created. “and all that are in them”: everything that was created.

“heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever.” They heard what John said, and they understood it, all the creatures.

That is why the land itself rejoices in Isaiah 35. The whole creation answers to the Lord, and when “the glory of Lebanon” is given and they “see the glory of the Lord, and the excellency of our God”, it is because the Lord will be on the earth, and everything will change.

thread.label: Ezekiel 20:35-38
thread.text: And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.

precepts.label: Hebrews 8:10-11
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”. The rod is correction. And the bond of the covenant is the new covenant in Hebrews: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord”. After those days means after we are delivered out of here, out of this new Egypt, America.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”. Meaning we are going to know God's laws and we will keep God's laws. Right now it can be routine: you go to work every day, stop in the donut store for a donut and your coffee, eat the donut, and then remember, damn, it's the days of unleavened bread, how could I forget? But the Lord God says his laws will be in our minds. We are not going to forget, and we will do them and serve him. That is the new covenant. We are in the beginning of it now, but once Christ returns it will be fully established in the wilderness.

“And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.” All of us will know the Lord, from the least amongst us to the greatest. You won't have to go and teach anybody, because the Lord is going to teach us. Every custom and thought we learned in America has to go, and he will show us even the parts we are missing now, like the sun and the moon working together for the times and seasons, wisdom destroyed from amongst us through slavery.

So being brought into the bond of the covenant is us being purged in the wilderness again. As he pleaded with our fathers and got rid of the leaven from amongst them, he will “purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”: those that break God's laws, those with leaven in them. Many will be delivered out of here, but not everyone is going to make it into the promised land. Those who enter will have his laws written in their hearts.

thread.label: Amos 4:5
thread.text: And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord God.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:6
precepts.why:
Amos rebukes Israel: “offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel”. Christ shows what that leaven is: “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees”.

The leaven of the Pharisees was hypocrisy; the leaven of the Pharisees is sin. Christ is saying, be careful of the sins of the Pharisees, for they say and do not. So the leaven in the scriptures is really going into sin, and leaven is not only bread with yeast in it; it is something much more symbolic.

That is what Amos exposes. We were offering our thanksgiving with leaven, with sin, and thinking that was acceptable to God. You cannot be in the midst of sin and give God thanks offerings. The Lord said, I don't work with that, I don't deal with that. That's how you black people is: in the midst of sin and coming to me with offerings.

So the days of unleavened bread we are celebrating represent us being without sin. The soul that has leaven in it for those seven days is cut off, and that is damnation. It is going into something much heavier: the days of unleavened bread are us fixing ourselves right now, getting rid of the leaven, the sins you are battling, trying to become a better person, so that when the Lord returns our souls are not cut off.

thread.label: Amos 9:9-10
thread.text: For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:6
precepts.why:
Amos says, “All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” That is what God said is going to happen, and there is nothing you can do to delay or undo it. So we have to come out of the beast; we have to come out of that mentality. Jeremiah says, “Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul”.

Flee out of Babylon can be physical. That day may come when we have to go to different lands: some of us will be exiles, some will be deported, and sometimes you may have to go to the next city or somewhere else to keep this gospel moving. But it is also spiritual: we have to flee out of the ways of the beast now.

“Deliver every man his soul”: the soul is the real you, underneath this sinful flesh, and the Lord is telling us to deliver it. That means letting go of the things we are accustomed to here. We cannot be like Lot's wife, who looked back and became a part of the Lord's sacrifice.

The Lord is giving us the place, the time and the opportunity to get ourselves right, but the day of the Lord is approaching regardless. Some carry the spirit of those who say the evil shall not overtake them: I am an Israelite, I don't have to worry, the Lord will give me mercy. We cannot roll in that mentality. If you fall, get back up immediately, because that mindset has this future. We are in the midst of a spiritual war, and we have to meditate on these things constantly, get our minds right and stay steadfast until the end.

precepts.label: Matthew 23:1-3
precepts.why:
Christ said, “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” What was the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees? Matthew 23 shows the first part of it.

“The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” They were hypocrites. What they said out of Moses' seat was the law, and that you do. But their works did not match their words.

“Do not ye after their works”, because their works were after someone else, and that is the rest of the leaven: who their works followed. The Passover reminds us that we were delivered because we were unleavened, righteous; so to be delivered again we have to move in the same spirit and purge the leaven out, not just check the box on the physical bread.

precepts.label: Mark 8:15
precepts.why:
Christ warned in Matthew 16 to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and in Matthew 23 he said to do what they bid from Moses' seat, but not after their works. Whose works were they following? Mark tells it: “And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.”

The leaven of Herod. That lets you know whose manner they were following: they were following the white man, Esau. That is why he tells us to beware.

So their leaven was not just being hypocrites. They were following after the manner of the wicked. Leaven is an influence that spreads, and when the rulers of Israel took on Herod's leaven, it spread through them; they came to move in the same spirit as the wicked they served. That is the warning to us: do not take on the leaven of Herod, the spirit of Esau, while wearing the garments of Israel.

precepts.label: John 11:45-48
precepts.why:
John 11 shows the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod at work. “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They believed on Christ.

“But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.” Wherever there is good, evil has to be there. You had the believers, and then you had coons set up there, running to tell.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” The Romans. That lets you know who their masters were and who they were following after. That is the leaven of Herod.

Leaven is an influence that spreads. That bitterness is on the inside, and it corrupts the spirit, the same bitterness that was in Cain toward Abel. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead to keep their place under Rome. If you are bitter toward your brother, you are in the same position as the scribes and Pharisees: the same spirit.

thread.label: Matthew 16:21-23
thread.text: From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.

precepts.label: Luke 4:13
precepts.why:
Christ told the disciples he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed and be raised again the third day. That was a good thing: he had to die to redeem the nation of Israel. But Peter took him and rebuked him: “Be it far from thee, Lord”. And Christ turned and said, “Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me”. What happened there? Satan literally jumped on Peter. That was not Peter; that was Satan talking to Christ through Peter, and Christ was talking to Satan.

Luke shows how that could be. After the temptation in the wilderness: “And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.” For a season. You think Satan stopped tempting Christ? He never stopped. He just left for a season and kept coming in different ways. When Christ was about to be crucified, Satan came back, and he came by jumping on Peter.

That is why Christ told Peter in another place that Satan desired to have him, to sift him as wheat, but that he had prayed for him that his faith fail not.

Satan comes for all of us; that is his job. For some it is money, for some it is sex, for some it is hatred. He comes at your weakness. So examine yourself: what is my weakness? That is what you need to strengthen, because that is what Satan will try to destroy you with. The worst are the ones who say they have no weakness; they deal with the heaviest demons and are just good at hiding it. The war is in your mind: when the evil thought comes, rebuke it, as Christ did: get thee behind me.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 16:14-16
precepts.why:
Mark 7:22 names “an evil eye” among the evil things that come “from within, out of the heart of men”, and “All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” 1 Samuel 18:9 says “Saul eyed David from that day and forward.” Was it with the looks of righteousness, or with an evil eye? An evil eye. And that evil eye defiled Saul even further, after the Lord had already rejected him. To see it, go back to where Saul’s trouble began, in chapter 16.

“But the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him.” Saul was already battling some things. The Lord had rejected him, and an evil spirit from the Lord had taken him.

“And Saul’s servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee. Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.” They told him: find someone who plays cunningly on a harp, and that spirit will leave you.

There are building blocks of bitterness. Bitterness doesn’t just come about; there are other things first. Saul rejected the word of the Lord, and the Spirit of the Lord departed from him. That was the ground the evil eye grew in. And don’t think, because you are not battling that spirit right now, that it won’t come. Satan says, hold my cup. Wait until you get the new job offer, the promotion, the demotion, the transfer to another school or another city, where you are dealing with different spirits and different circumstances, and you wonder why you are being troubled in the spirit. If it had not been for the Lord, we would all be as Sodom.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 16:23
precepts.why:
“And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.”

So David did a good thing by playing the music to have that spirit depart from King Saul. Saul did what the servants said, the spirit left him, and he was refreshed. He was like, man, I needed that. He was back in the spirit again. David was sent for Saul’s benefit, and Saul could not see it.

Now fast forward to chapter 18. Saul “eyed David from that day and forward”, and “it came to pass on the morrow, that the evil spirit from God came upon Saul.” The very next day after he had an evil eye towards David, meaning he was ready to do harm to David, that evil spirit returned. “And David played with his hand, as at other times: and there was a javelin in Saul’s hand.” David had already done this for him, as at other times. “And Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it.”

That is how quickly hatred can progress: the man whose playing made the evil spirit depart becomes the target of the javelin. That is Mark 7: “an evil eye” comes from within and defiles the man. The evil eye brought the evil spirit back, and the bitterness turned into an attempt to kill.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 5:6-7
precepts.why:
Christ likens the kingdom to leaven hid in three measures of meal “till the whole was leavened.” Leaven grows. Paul shows the other side of that same truth: “Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?” Because leaven grows, if you allow it to remain amongst other Israelites, that leaven is going to spread and defile others.

So the command is “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.” We have to purge out the leaven within our own spirits and within our various congregations. God purged you from your old sins, but if you don't keep trimming, if you don't keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly.

“For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ was sacrificed for us, so we no longer live unto ourselves; now we live unto Christ. This is a wake-up call, a readjustment, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness and stop it.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:6-12
precepts.why:
“Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” Christ was warning the twelve of the leaven. Christ was the leader, and when leaders try to warn you of leaven, you need to listen. He knew what he was talking about.

The disciples “reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have taken no bread.” No, he was not talking about bread. He reminded them of “the five loaves of the five thousand” and “the seven loaves of the four thousand”: it's not about the bread, pay attention. They couldn't receive it at that time, until “Then understood they how that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” The leaven is their doctrine and their sinful nature. Don't get caught up in the things they do: they say and do not, they are hypocrites.

And the Pharisees and the Sadducees were Israelites. That doesn't mean we have anything against anybody, but when you see a spirit on someone who can influence you negatively, beware. It's up to you to listen, but the best thing is to follow, listen and consider the end of their conversation. Be very, very mindful.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 2:11
precepts.why:
“Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” Every year the Passover comes around and we see the same thing happen: people start bugging out. And people who have been with us, who saw it happen before, still fall for it. We have to fight. Don't play into Satan's devices.

He wants you right where he's got you. Some are on their way out because they're not paying attention to class, not studying, not praying, not getting their four chapters, not doing anything right. Satan has you right where he wants you.

We should not be ignorant of his devices, but some remain ignorant, and the reason is that they despise wisdom and don't want to be taught. That is how the leaven gets in and spreads.

precepts.label: Sirach 21:12
precepts.why:
Some don't want to be taught, and Sirach says why: “He that is not wise will not be taught”. If you're a fool, it doesn't matter what somebody does for you; you will not be taught, you will not retain it, it's not going to work for you.

“but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness”. That wisdom is seeing it your own way, doing your own thing, and you're going to have a bitter end because of it.

Sirach 3:26 shows that bitterness: “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last”. You're stubborn and don't want to learn; when wise words come out you're in the back, or you've got that hatred, something against somebody, so you don't want to hear nothing from them. And “he that loveth danger shall perish therein”. People like that are very dangerous; they can get people hurt if you follow after them. They perish in their folly, because they are unwise and not taught, because fools despise knowledge.

precepts.label: Sirach 10:12
precepts.why:
This tends to happen every year around the Passover, and this is a call to wake some up so they can get their mind right. “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”. When you notice that your study habits have changed, when you notice that you're pulling back from the believers, understand that pride has now set in. You are regressing, going backwards.

“and his heart is turned away from his Maker”. That sin, that leaven, is now blinding you, so that you can no longer see clearly. That is the leaven spreading through the whole lump: it starts small, with a pulling back, and grows until the heart is turned away from the Most High.

precepts.label: Hebrews 3:13
precepts.why:
“But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day”. How often? Daily. Exhortation can't take place if you're not around nobody. The Bible is telling us what to do: stay around each other, stay around the righteous daily.

“lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin”. Sin may feel good, but it's a deceiver, because you think you can get that feeling constantly. You can't; it's temporal, only for a certain amount of time. If we pull away, sin can take over our mind and we may never recover. That's the scary part.

2 Thessalonians 2 shows it. “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: America came after the workings of Satan, making you think God is with them, and it's time to come up out of the beast and separate. “And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.” They loved their pleasures more than God, deceived by the pleasures of sin. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion”. You can be deceived by sin so bad you may never recover your soul: still alive, still living, but a dead soul and a dead spirit. Be very mindful.

precepts.label: Tobit 6:10-17
precepts.why:
“But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin”. The thoughts warring against your mind are Satan, and one of the ways he brings you into the captivity of bitterness is over who is talking to whom. Brothers stop talking to a brother because of a sister. Two sisters were cool, both liked the same brother, and now they have stopped talking to each other. That is bitterness, and that is fake.

Tobit shows how God brings people together. The angel told Tobias, “to day we shall lodge with Raguel, who is thy cousin; he also hath one only daughter, named Sara; I will speak for her, that she may be given thee for a wife. For to thee doth the right of her appertain, seeing thou only art of her kindred.” And he told him, when he came into the marriage chamber and made the smoke, “the devil shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more”, and they should rise up both of them and pray to God.

Then: “fear not, for she is appointed unto thee from the beginning”. From ever since the beginning, that was his wife. The Most High does bring people together. If that brother is for you, he is for you. Whoever is for you is for you.

So do not develop bitterness and hatred toward each other over who is talking to whom. Be happy for the brother; be happy for the sister. You brothers cannot stop talking to each other because of a woman, and brothers who roll like that need to repent. That bitterness is going to change you, and it is just a matter of time before you leave the body. “With the mind I myself serve the law of God”: when those evil thoughts about your brother or sister come, shake them off.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:9
precepts.why:
Paul says, “be not conformed to this world”, because of who rules over this world: the white man. Don't have the mind of the Edomite, the mind of Cain. Instead, “be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”, after Christ. Just before, Ephesians told us, “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” That is what we have to do. But how do we really go about doing it?

David asks the same question: “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way?” How can we cleanse our ways? “by taking heed thereto according to thy word.”

The renewing of the mind comes by the word. We have to take heed according to the word, and that is how the bitter spirit, the leaven of Cain and Esau, is cleansed out, so that we may prove “what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:1-2
precepts.why:
Peter shows what the renewing of the mind looks like: “Wherefore laying aside all malice.” Lay aside all malice, family: all malice, all leaven. “and all guile”: that is the fake talk, because you are bitter. “and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings.” We have to lay these things aside.

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.” We have to be born again in Christ like newborn babes. The sincere milk of the word is the thing we have to desire, and it is what makes us grow.

This is Romans 12:2 at work. Being conformed to this world is carrying the mind of Cain and Esau: the malice, the guile, the envy and the evil speaking of the bitter spirit. Being transformed is laying all of that aside and feeding on the word until the mind is renewed after Christ.

precepts.label: James 1:21-24
precepts.why:
James tells us what to put off and what to take in: “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The word received with meekness is what saves the soul.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” We have to be doers of the word, family. We hear the class about putting away all bitterness, and then we don't do it.

“For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” When you read the scriptures, you see yourself in them. But after you read them, you go your way and don't really address the matter.

We don't want to do that. We want to examine ourselves, look to the scriptures and say: Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit. I'm bitter toward my wife, I'm bitter toward the leadership, I'm bitter toward my brother. We have to confess that thing and pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is being transformed by the renewing of the mind, and not conformed to this world.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:21
precepts.why:
“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. What is the example that Christ left? Peter: “For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps”.

Christ suffered for us: that goes back to him being our Passover, sacrificed for us. And he left an example, so as believers in Christ we must follow his steps. Christ came to bring peace. Bitterness does not do that.

So we apply the scriptures. Purge out the old sin, the old man, that we may be a new lump, a new creature in Christ, following in the steps of Christ. “Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness”. That malice is the bitterness: a dumb thought jumps in, the seed gets planted, it gets nourished, and next thing you know you have malice, hatred toward your brother, and wickedness, because it leads to sin.

“but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth”. Meaning: I have the bitter spirit, so I have to go to my brother and talk to him in sincerity and truth. Brothers sweep under the floor mats and dump out the toaster at Passover, and there is not a grain of yeast in the house, while they carry an evil eye toward a brother or bitterness toward a wife. We are the temple of God; the leaven has to come out of the spirit.

And do not tuck it away for later, like the brother who puts the bread in the storage closet during the feast and brings it back when the season is over. Following Christ's steps means letting the bitterness go entirely.

precepts.label: Proverbs 22:24-25
precepts.why:
“evil communications corrupt good manners.” Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes things rise, and that is what bitterness does. The root of bitterness corrupts your spirit and messes with your attitude, and that angry influence spreads to others through words and through attitude.

So Proverbs warns: “Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go”. You see that brother is bitter; he is like that dangerous overgrown brush. There could be a viper in there, anything on the other side of that bush. Move.

“Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.” Now that bitter brother has put the bitter spirit on you. You got bit, like Bird Box, and now you are looking dumb. That is the snare right there.

That is why the scripture says be not deceived. Keeping company with the bitter brother is how the leaven gets into you. His evil communications will corrupt your good manners, and his offenses will reach others, starting with the first offense, the one in your own house.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 4:18
thread.text: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:4
precepts.why:
“for the things which are seen are temporal”: the things we see now are temporary. They are not going to last forever, so there is no need for us to get caught up in the things of the world. The United States of America is the world superpower and influences the whole world. Whatever music is played in America, whatever is in pop culture, the whole world responds to it. But this regime, this power, will fall, thus saith the Lord. Now we have to put our focus on overcoming the beast.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”. Anybody in this war against evil does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life, “that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” Who chose us? Our Lord and Saviour, Jesus the Christ. He chose us to be soldiers in his military.

When Ezekiel saw that exceeding great army, he saw purple and gold. Who else is out there as foot soldiers, going nation to nation, island to island, land to land, teaching the word of God? It is not to boast; it is just the reality.

So a soldier keeps his eyes on what is not seen. We do not see the kingdom right now, but the Lord lets us know it will last forever. The Lord is doing his job; it is time for us to do ours.

precepts.label: Romans 12:2
precepts.why:
“the things which are not seen are eternal” We do not see the kingdom yet, but it will last forever. So we have to stack our bricks, and we cannot be situational Israelites. We have to be in the spirit and move in the spirit, knowing our eternal home awaits us. It is a spiritual battle, a spiritual war.

“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. We have to change by the renewing of our minds, because we are now new creatures in Christ. The mindset has to change.

Those things that used to trip us up so often and so easily in the world, in this day and age, cannot keep doing it. If you feel Satan raising up his head against you, if you feel that old man coming back, you have to do any and everything to deaden that spirit. Now ain't the time for that.

That is what it means to look not at the things which are seen. The world presses its pop culture and pleasures on us, but a mind renewed stays fixed on the eternal kingdom rather than conforming to a power that is about to fall.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:1
precepts.why:
“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight”: everything that is trying to keep us from serving our God. That is exactly what sin does. “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” The earthly tabernacle is our flesh. We were born and shapen in iniquity, so understand the condition of the battle: we will fight against our flesh until we die or until Christ returns.

A lot of people think that when they come into the truth, things will just go away. Some things you stop doing: eating pork, breaking the Lord's Sabbath, not wearing fringes, shaving your beard. You start keeping the commandments, your reasonable service. But hatred, lust and covetousness do not go away. You learn how to cope with them, and you have to prove yourself to the Lord that you are able to keep that Negro in check, that Latino in check.

“and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us”. We do not have a lot of time left. Now is high time to wake up out of sleep and fight this battle right here. We are not worried about the war in Iran; God already has that. We need to worry about the war on the day-to-day.

That is looking at the things which are not seen: running the race with patience toward the eternal, not weighed down by the temporal.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 7:31
precepts.why:
This kingdom will go down. It will pass away just like everything else. “And they that use this world, as not abusing it: for the fashion of this world passeth away.” You can use the things of this world, but do not get caught up. Do not hit the snooze button, do not abuse it, and do not lean on the things of this world over Christ.

If we really believe this Bible, we know the things of this world are going to pass away, and that fear should kick in on its own. Someone should not always have to check you. You read the Bible just like the next man. We understand young spirits, but eventually, as you walk, you check yourself.

You should become skilful in the word of God. “Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding standing, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast.” If wisdom is walking with you, if Christ is in you, by default you become skilful in the word and in how to apply wisdom in certain situations. You embody Christ, and everybody can see wisdom walking with you.

So the things seen are temporal and the fashion of this world passes away, while the things not seen are eternal. Use the world lightly and hold fast to wisdom.

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:28-31
precepts.why:
Paul says “the sorrow of the world worketh death.” Here is what that worldly sorrow looks like: “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me”. When the Lord increases the affliction, after you have been wicked the whole time, now you are calling on the Lord: it's getting real down here, the persecution is on, I ain't got no food. You call, and the line says the number you have dialed is no longer available to you, dummy. You'll seek him early, like getting on a pre-call, and you still won't find him. You won't have any connection to the Lord on that day.

Why? “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. They had the carnal mind, the mind of Cain and Esau, and cast the word behind their back like their father did. “They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.” They literally threw the word behind their back, and a lot of our brothers and sisters do that. We all have to examine ourselves.

“Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.” If you are out there sowing sin, that is what you are going to reap.

That is Esau's sorrow. He sold his birthright, then realized, damn, I want that blessing back, and cried bitterly over what he himself threw away. So we have to be sincere when we come to the Lord and have the real godly sorrow that works repentance to salvation, to our inheritance, not to be repented of. We can't be out here faking the funk.

precepts.label: Proverbs 14:10
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves”: not your neighbor, yourself. And you can do it, because “The heart knoweth his own bitterness”. Your mind knows its own bitterness. Brother, sister, you can't play confused when somebody asks, man, where is that bitterness coming from?

“and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.” So you can't say, oh Bishop, tell me what's going on with me. You know exactly what is going on in your mind. Nobody else can get in and decipher exactly what it is. We can say, brother, you're off, you ain't moving right, there is sin in there; we may not know it specifically, but you know the specifics of what you are dealing with.

This is a heavy topic. A lot of brothers and sisters are bitter. It came up in our congregation with a brother dealing with his wife, and then we came down here and saw the same thing, and it destroyed a household. If that spirit is left unchecked it can destroy the congregation. That is why each of us has to prove our own self: the heart already knows where the bitterness is.

precepts.label: Psalms 139:23-24
precepts.why:
To examine ourselves we ask the Lord to do it with us: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me”. We ask the Lord to reveal the iniquity in us and not leave us blind to our own folly.

How is he going to do that? When you say, Lord, search me, that means you have to search the scriptures. The Lord ain't going to come down and say, open that door right there, let me see what's behind it. No, brother. You have to search the scriptures.

Then, in order to get over the root of bitterness, we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. We look to the scriptures and say, Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit, bitter toward my wife, toward the leadership, toward my brother, and we pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is how we prove our own selves, whether we be in the faith.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 10:13
precepts.why:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man.” Bitterness is a very common thing that many of us battle with. We are never alone in it: if leadership sees a spirit in one congregation, they have to understand that the same spirit is elsewhere. That is the “one body, and one Spirit” of Ephesians 4:4. The classes are not rehearsed, yet the same talking points come out in different places, because the Lord puts the spirit on the leadership to address the prevalent issue of the time, and in the midst of Passover He revealed bitterness throughout the congregations.

“But God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” Even while being tried and tempted, the Lord in His faithfulness makes a way out.

What is the way to escape? Put a class on. Call a brother. Speak to your brother, to get that spirit off of you. A lot of times the devil jumps on us and we start battling in our own mind, and we create a whole other reality that does not even exist in real life. You talk to the brother and you say, damn, all that mess I was thinking and rehearsing is not even the case.

That matters, because bitterness is the hidden leaven that must be purged. If it is not purged, it grows into a root that defiles the soul. Many brothers who left the body and came out with crazy videos started with a root of bitterness.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:12-13
precepts.why:
Ephesians 4 says what to put away: “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” Bitterness comes first, and the rest come along with it: wrath, anger, clamour, and evil speaking, talking foolish and reckless about the brother, the sister, your wife. That thing has to be put away with extreme hatred. Instead: “be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.” You want to seek pardon from the Lord, but you have hatred toward your brother?

Colossians says what to put on in its place: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” That is how we have to move. The elect of God forbear and forgive one another.

Offenses are going to come in the congregation: a brother says something, a sister says something, and somebody gets offended. We all have to have mercy on one another, because we are all sick. This is a hospital. If a brother coughs on you, you forgive the brother, because everybody in here is sick.

This is how the bitter leaven gets purged. It came up in one congregation where a brother was bitter with his wife and it destroyed a household, and the same spirit showed up elsewhere. Left unchecked, it can destroy a congregation, so we put off the bitterness and put on mercy and forgiveness, as Christ forgave us.
