precepts.label: 1 John 3:8-10
precepts.why:
Hebrews warns of the “root of bitterness springing up”, and John shows what spirit jumps on you when you move that way. “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” That is the history being drawn out from Cain to Esau: the devil sinned from the beginning, and the same spirit runs down through his children.

“For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.” The purpose of Christ is to destroy the works of the devil. So why do we move in the spirit of the devil and think that we are moving in the spirit of Christ?

“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God.” This is the manifestation of the children of God. If you don't do righteousness, you are not of God. The scripture tells us how to deal uprightly with our brother and sister: if there is an offense, go by Matthew 18:15. You don't sow discord and murmur in the midst of the congregation and spread that spirit through our brothers and sisters.

“neither he that loveth not his brother.” When you don't love your brother, you are not moving in the spirit of Christ and you are not counted a child of God. You are the son and daughter of Cain, of Esau. We have to be mindful of this spirit and purge that leaven, that bitter spirit, out of us.

precepts.label: Romans 8:6-7
precepts.why:
Esau was a man of the field and a profane person: his religion is sin. Paul gives the name for that mind: “For to be carnally minded is death.” To be carnally minded is to be Edomite minded, the profane mind. It is death, and that is why he is called the son of perdition.

“but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” When you are spiritually minded, you say, I have to gain my brother. That does not mean we always have to be buddy-buddy, but the scripture says instead of a friend become not an enemy. Brothers turn a brother into an enemy like a rival team in sports, stay pumped up against him and hold on to that feeling, waiting to get back at him. That is the carnal mind. Stay in the spirit.

“Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God.” The Edomite mind, the mind of the spirit of Cain, goes against God and is not subject to his law.

So there are the children of God and the children of the devil, with no in between: either the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The bitter spirit that holds a grudge against a brother is the carnal mind of Esau, and it leads to the same death and rejection he found.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:16-17
precepts.why:
This is the Edomite mindset, the carnal mind at war with God. “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Unto the wicked, the white man, God says: hold on, you are carnally minded. Why are you out there talking about in God we trust? Why are you swearing in on the Bible when you do nothing according to the scriptures?

“Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” He talks about in God we trust while he has transgenders out there, putting two men together. They don't do anything the scriptures say. They cast the word behind their back, because the carnal mind is at war with God.

This is the battle of the spirit and the flesh, and that inner battle is within us too. It is the same profane spirit Hebrews names in Esau, whose religion is sin and who despised what was sacred. So we have to make sure we stand in the spirit, and not take God's covenant in our mouth while we cast his words behind us, as a brother does when he holds on to a bitter spirit.

thread.text: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:

precepts.label: Matthew 5:28
precepts.why:
“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin.” Where is lust conceived? In your mind; that is where the root begins. Christ shows exactly how: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” That is how lust is conceived.

We are living in an evil world, and we all see beautiful women. A picture of an immodestly dressed woman was put on the screen and the brothers were asked one by one what they saw. One liked the way she dressed. Another said she is beautiful, but the way she dresses you have to hate that thing, she has to be modest. Another said, I have been in the world a lot longer than in the truth, so I am working on hating it. What you see on the screen you see every damn day when you go outside, and some of you break your neck walking down the street.

You have to train yourself to hate evil. It doesn’t come naturally; you cannot come to the truth and all of a sudden hate what you see out there. When you see her, train your mind: she has AIDS, she stinks, she has to be a man. If you don’t, you will always be watching and desiring these things. Older brothers with experience have matured past it; the young brothers dealing with youthful lusts have to train. Sisters, before the truth many of you walked around in miniskirts and spandex, giggling and giving out your number to every dude on the block, and now you have changed how you dress. When Christ returns there will be a modesty law set up.

So you see it, and in your mind you say, damn, I don’t mind sleeping with that. When you allow that thought, lust is conceived, and sin comes forth. But if the thought comes and you shake it off, what’s wrong with you, God is going to kill you, stop thinking like that, it is not conceived. If you sit down and entertain it, it brings forth sin. That is why Christ says adultery doesn’t start when you literally lie down with a woman; it starts in your mind. “and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” Some say I fornicated and I didn’t die; that death is damnation, your soul being destroyed. God will judge you.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 21:27
precepts.why:
John says “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Even the scribes and Pharisees took on the spirit of Cain, of Satan; they moved in the same exact spirit, bitter toward Christ and wanting to put him to death. That spirit will jump on us too, and we have to deal with it. When we are overcome with it, we take on the same attributes Cain did.

“When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” You will have brothers and sisters say, the white man is the devil, they're going to be destroyed, they're going into captivity. And meanwhile you are moving in the same spirit. So you curse Satan, and you curse your own soul, because you have hatred toward your brother. Brothers talk bold against the white man and find themselves in the same spirit as him.

“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.” Whoever is bitter toward his brother is in the spirit of Cain; you are in the same spirit. That hatred is always masked: “Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” He acted like his friend to get him in position.

So we have to exercise ourselves to have a conscience void of offence. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God. Don't allow it to fester and resonate in your spirit until you are overcome, because “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren.”

thread.label: Revelation 13:1-6
thread.text: And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 28:3
precepts.why:
The beast has “upon his heads the name of blasphemy”, and “he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven”: the Most High, Christ and the angels. That is what they do: they lie against God’s people and God himself. “The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.”

Look at the Tomahawk missile that hit the elementary school in Minab, Iran, killing 175 people, mostly children. First they blamed Iran; then they said it was a mistake from outdated targeting data; then Trump said, I don’t know about it. Don’t listen for one second to these liars.

Ezekiel 28:3 answers them: “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”. What was Daniel able to do? Interpret dreams. America is able to interpret your next move, because they have that kind of surveillance and technological capability. The Bible prophesied it.

So if there is no secret that can be hid from America, according to God, how did they mistakenly hit a school and think it was part of a base? It was no mistake. It shows you they are crooks and liars, the beast with a mouth speaking blasphemies. And to our people still asleep and following behind the beast, even a ranking man among us who re-enlisted in the army in the middle of Bible prophecy, knowing he will be deployed: come up out of this foolishness.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:3
precepts.why:
The beast of Revelation 13 rises out of the sea “having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns”. The seven heads are Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain. The ten horns are the ten common markets, the EU, and on the military side NATO, now over thirty nations.

Revelation 12:3 shows the same creature: “And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” This heaven is rulership: who would be leading the earth, the world superpower, in the latter days. So the beast is also the red dragon, and red is the key indicator of who this is.

Genesis 25:25 tells you: “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Then “after that came his brother out”, with no description at all. Why? Because Jacob looked just like everybody else; everybody at that time had dark pigmentation. Esau was different, so he had to be described.

So the great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns is Esau, and the beast in power in the latter days is America, of the seven because the Americans came over here from Great Britain, with the ten horns giving their power and strength to it.

thread.label: Revelation 17:1-18
thread.text: And there came one of the seven angels which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters:

precepts.label: Romans 13:11
precepts.why:
The ten horns “have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast.” That is NATO, formed in 1949, with America at the front. But things are changing. France and Italy are negotiating with Iran for oil through the Strait of Hormuz; Canada says it will never take part in the offensive; Germany warns against an endless war; Spain has withdrawn its ambassador from Israel. They agreed to give their power to the beast, and now they are looking out for themselves.

So as Israelites, the blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans scattered abroad, not only here in America, when we see things like this we have to understand our salvation is getting closer. “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”: nearer than when we first came to the knowledge. Things are escalating rather quickly, and this conflict is something to keep our eyes on.

A lot of us do not recognize what the feast of Passover is really about: the destruction of our enemies and us being saved from their hands. How fitting that the high holy day comes in a time like this. So we have to increase our focus and buckle down; we are in the midst of war, and our minds should not be in other places.

As Deacon Yashua in Phoenix said last Sabbath: prophecy should move us to correction; it is not for our entertainment.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1-2
precepts.why:
“And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” Over time something will cause these kings to hate the whore, the United States of America. Trump badmouths NATO for not paying their fees and threatens to end the alliance, and now they don’t want to be drawn into a long war. They will make her desolate and naked with intercontinental ballistic missiles.

But before that comes, we have to achieve abstinence, discipline, overcoming, and unity. Zephaniah says: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”. The nation not desired is us. They call us minorities and put labels on us, blacks, Hispanics, derogatory terms wherever we are: the Dalits in India, the Afro-Iranians, the Afro-Palestinians. Wherever we are scattered we are hated and despised. But the Bible says gather together. It is all about Israelite unity, and that is what they have always feared, because if the Israelites unify, that is the end of this wicked regime.

They even lie about Amalek. Bibi Netanyahu and his crew are the Amalekites according to the Bible, so to deflect that history they call the Iranians, the Persians, present-day Amalek.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you”. The decree is already made; it is prophesied, and destruction is coming. So take heed, acknowledge it, and get yourselves right.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:9-11
precepts.why:
Zephaniah speaks of the decree; Peter shows it will not fail: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness”. What the Lord said is exactly what will come to pass. He “is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” The Lord does not want any of his people to perish, and that is why he is giving us time to get ourselves right. That does not mean he will not put the wicked to death.

“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”, whether you get yourself right or not, “in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. How is that possible? By nuclear fire: the same burning with fire the ten horns bring on the whore.

“Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be”? That goes to Deacon Yashua’s point. Should we sit with the popcorn just watching? Eating popcorn is not a sin, with a little butter and salt. But if that is all you are doing and you are not applying, that is when it becomes an issue.

This is not the time to kick our feet up or bug out. Now is the time to work like we never worked before and to increase in righteousness.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 1:9
precepts.why:
The Lord says, “I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction. For wickedness hath exceedingly polluted the whole earth”. How did wickedness come to pollute the whole earth? Esau. Malachi calls Edom the border of wickedness, and since the time of the Greeks that wickedness has grown and grown.

After Alexander the Greek died, “they all put crowns upon themselves; so did their sons after them many years: and evils were multiplied in the earth.” That is the spread of it: from the Greeks all the way up until today. Do not forget the Romans, Spain, France, Germany, Great Britain, Russia and the United States of America. Each put crowns on themselves, their sons after them, and evils were multiplied.

That is why “their hurtful works are fulfilled”, and why the plagues are coming on the world. Every nation on the face of the earth has been affected by that line of kingdoms, now by America, by Edom. The whole world is defiled because of it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:1-2
precepts.why:
The earth is under much wickedness, in gross darkness. Isaiah says, “Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” Arise: awake to righteousness; it is time to wake up out of that deep sleep. Shine: that is going out to teach, letting your light shine, teaching God's commandments. Our light is Christ.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. The darkness covering the earth is the nations: every nation is affected by the United States of America, by Edom, and the whole world is defiled because of this nation. And because of that, the Israelites have been affected: gross darkness the people, God's people.

Then: “but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” The Lord is still going to arise upon us, because he is still going to choose Israel and have mercy on his people: the ones who want to stop sinning, not the ones who take advantage of God's grace and mercy. His glory shall be seen upon his people.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:7
precepts.why:
The earth is polluted with wickedness, and Babylon is at the center of it. “How much she hath glorified herself, and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her: for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.”

America really thinks it will never have to pay for its crimes. So if you are sitting in your sins thinking, as Amos 9:10 says, that no harm is going to come to you, you have a characteristic of Edom, the same characteristic as Esau. If we want deliverance, why would we have that mentality? We cannot get salvation unless she is destroyed. So if you want to remain in your sins, you want America to continue.

This is for the brothers and sisters you barely ever see, because they always have something more important than the truth; the ones who fade, and nobody hears from them. This is a gut check, so you can get your mind right. Some of you have embodied the characteristics of America, and it is time to shake that off.

A lot of us look at America as a gorgeous, beautiful woman and are mesmerized. But she is the mother of harlots, and just because you are not picking up a prostitute does not mean you are not out there dealing with harlots. She lives deliciously and thinks she will see no sorrow, but so much torment and sorrow will be given her. Come out of her.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 15:7-12
thread.text: Therefore saith the Lord,

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 13:3
precepts.why:
Ezra says the Lord will not suffer his people “now to dwell in the land of Egypt”, but will “smite Egypt with plagues, as before”. As before means this is not ancient Egypt; it is a coming Egypt, the United States of America. When it comes, we don't want to go down with it. So why would our people love this Egypt? Because of her beauty.

Wisdom answers: “With whose beauty if they being delighted took them to be gods; let them know how much better the Lord of them is: for the first author of beauty hath created them.”

The first author of beauty is our God. Real beauty is not the Statue of Liberty; that is not real beauty. Only virgins are really beautiful. God is the creator of beauty, and he looked at us as beautiful. That is why he refers to us as a woman, as Jeremiah 6:2 shows.

So in this Passover season, get your mind right and remove the leaven. Do not be delighted with the beauty of Egypt and take her for a god. Know how much better the Lord is, who made the beauty.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 6:2
precepts.why:
The first author of beauty is our God, and he looked at us as beautiful. That is why he refers to us as a woman: “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.”

Comely means beautiful, handsome. That is how the Lord looks at his people: the daughter of Zion is a comely and delicate woman in his eyes.

That is why he says in 2 Esdras that “the innocent and righteous blood crieth unto me”, that “my people is led as a flock to the slaughter”, and that he will surely avenge them. All the murders and injustice done to God's children here in spiritual Egypt are done to the daughter he likened to a comely and delicate woman, and he will not suffer them to dwell in that Egypt any more.

precepts.label: Lamentations 2:1
precepts.why:
The Lord likened the daughter of Zion to a comely woman, yet Jeremiah laments: “How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!”

The Lord cast the beauty of Israel down from heaven, from rulership, to the earth, to servitude. Why would he do that? Because we went off. We went away from the author who created us. That is why you would look to another nation for its beauty.

But God is letting you know he is the author, the creator of beauty. And America, that you think is beautiful, really is not beautiful. Under the skirt she is a worn-out harlot: you think she is beautiful, then you realize she has been with everyone on the block.

You went against your God. So now, knowing that, we have to return. We have to return back to the author of our beauty, so that he will avenge us and bring us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.

precepts.label: Psalms 45:7-11
precepts.why:
The beauty of Israel was cast down because we left our God, so now we have to return. David shows how: “Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” We have to love righteousness and hate iniquity.

“All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces”, and “upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir.”

“Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house”. The Lord says listen up. Just like a marriage, sisters, you have to focus on your lord. The Lord does not want to share us with anybody else; he wants us to focus on him and him only.

“So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.” When we get ourselves right, turn back to the Lord, love righteousness and hate iniquity, he will desire our beauty, the way he created it. And we worship him and him only, not the beauty of Egypt.

thread.label: Sirach 4:11
thread.text: Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:24
precepts.why:
“Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.” Who is this wisdom we are to seek? Christ is also known as wisdom: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

So when Sirach speaks of wisdom exalting her children, and when Proverbs has wisdom saying “By me princes rule”, it is Christ speaking. The Lord is the one who sets up all the kings and all the princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God by whom they rule.

To seek wisdom is to seek Christ. Those who seek him are the ones wisdom lays hold of, and the children she exalts are the ones he calls: the called, both Jews and Greeks.

precepts.label: Proverbs 8:16-19
precepts.why:
How do we seek wisdom? Wisdom answers in Proverbs: “By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth.” The Lord sets up all the kings and princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God.

“I love them that love me”: the Lord only loves those who love him. If you are not seeking him, he does not love you. “and those that seek me early shall find me.” We have a chance right now, in the midst of these wars and rumours of wars: we have to seek the Lord early, right now.

“Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness.” Riches and honour are with Christ. Durable riches are not temporal, not temporary; they last a long time, forever, eternal. “My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.”

That is how wisdom exalts her children and lays hold of them that seek her: she loves those who love her, she is found by those who seek her early, and she gives them lasting riches and righteousness.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 3:3-13
precepts.why:
We have to be like Solomon: we have to pray for wisdom so that we can be increased. “And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the statutes of David his father”, and at Gibeon “the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.”

Solomon answered, “I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in”, set in the midst of “a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.” “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad”. As a youth, Solomon understood that wisdom was important. He could have asked for a lot of different things, but he asked for wisdom.

“And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.” Because he “hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies”, God gave him “a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.” And more: “I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour”.

The Lord gave Solomon things he did not ask for because he asked for the right thing. We can desire different pleasures of lust, but seek ye first the kingdom of heaven and everything else will be added to us. Take a page out of Solomon’s book: wisdom exalted him because he sought her.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13
precepts.why:
Solomon tells it himself: “For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out. Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.”

“I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” So the question is: do you prefer God’s wisdom? Do you prefer the Lord over your sensual desires? “all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her. I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” Solomon did not care about anything else except wisdom.

“All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands. And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them”. Wisdom goes before everything.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” He did not hide his wisdom. Sirach says the same: “refrain not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not thy wisdom in her beauty.” Just as Bishop gets on us all the time, our communication should be in the scriptures. Searching after wisdom is a good thing; that is what we are supposed to do. That is how we should talk, it should be on our minds at all times, and everything should always go back to the scriptures.

precepts.label: James 1:5-6
precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If we lack wisdom, go to the source: go to the Father in the name of the Son, Jesus the Christ.

Sirach shows how wisdom deals with the one who seeks her: “For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.” When we come into this truth we are not right, so wisdom walks with us in our crooked ways, and the Lord will jack us up because we are not doing it right; but wisdom will still be there. “Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.” There is no cap on wisdom.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” That is the key: you have to believe. “But without faith it is impossible to please him”. Without Christ it is impossible to please the Father, so we must build our faith. And “faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” We have to increase our study as we see the days approaching, and continue to converse in the scriptures.

precepts.label: Psalms 103:13
precepts.why:
“Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.” The Lord will have mercy and pity on those who fear him: not the unfaithful, but those who fear him. They are wisdom’s children.

Isaiah shows what that pity does: “for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.” The Lord will fight those who fought against us, and he will save our children, because wisdom exalts her children.

He does it through Christ: “behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH”, and “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.” That is what it pays to be faithful and diligent: the Lord will pardon our iniquity and remove it.

And the end of it is in Revelation: “the accuser of our brethren is cast down”, and “they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.” We overcome by the blood of the Lamb; we must have faith and continue to be faithful, loving righteousness more than iniquity. The Father pities his children who fear him, and exalts them.

thread.label: Sirach 25:21
thread.text: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 3:1-4
precepts.why:
“Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.” Many of you look at America as a gorgeous, beautiful woman, and you are mesmerized. In America you can have every kind of pleasure. A lot of brothers fall by harlots, and just because you are not picking up a prostitute doesn’t mean you aren’t out there dealing with harlots. This is the mother of all harlots. And remember, sin is pleasurable.

Paul describes the last days: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection”: some like young minors, some like people of the same sex. “Trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good.” I don’t like that brother. Why not? Every time I look up he is doing something. What, teaching the word of God? We have spirits like that sitting among us, worried about petty things while this truth is trying to get us out of here.

“Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.” That is a big issue. If you love pleasure more than you love God, you start making excuses to feed that lust, and you find yourself not around doing the Lord’s work as much. Everybody asks, what’s wrong with that brother’s spirit? He loves his lust more than God.

That is what it means to stumble at the beauty of the woman and desire her for pleasure: to love America’s pleasures more than God. The brothers and sisters who fade away, this is your gut check.

precepts.label: Hebrews 11:24-25
precepts.why:
Don’t stumble at the beauty of the woman, America, or desire her for pleasure. Moses shows the way: “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.” He wanted nothing to do with Egypt or the king of Egypt, because he knew he was an Israelite and God had chosen him for a mighty work, to deliver his people out of captivity.

Some of y’all say, it’s not that bad, and you show it by your mentality and your actions. Moses lived it up and had status in Egypt, like some of you have nice jobs and status in America. So you can’t say it’s because of that. Moses gave it all up; why can’t you?

“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” For a season means it is temporary. It is only here for so long, and then destruction and salvation. That is the mindset we have to have.

We have to be robotic and get the feelings out of it. Nobody cares how you feel; feelings get you killed. Choose affliction with the people of God over the passing pleasures of Babylon.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:19
precepts.why:
The class is The Beauty and the Beast, and this is the beauty. When sin takes over, you can’t see clearly. Isaiah says: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency.” That is how they perceive her, and how many of our people see America.

But you shouldn’t look at America like that. When you see the Statue of Liberty, you shouldn’t say, God bless America. Some of y’all feel real proud seeing things like that. When I first looked at it, I saw seven crowns on her head and ten toes, and I said, wow, the Bible is a true book. Not, Lady Liberty, I love you. The Bible is spot on.

“Shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” This place is going to be destroyed. You shouldn’t be sitting there gazing at her and mesmerized by her pleasures. You know this place is coming to an end. Wake up. Don’t stumble at her beauty.

precepts.label: Nahum 3:4
precepts.why:
Sirach warns not to stumble at the beauty of a woman, and the Lord calls this nation a harlot. Nahum says: “Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts.” The well-favoured harlot: some of you are caught up with her. I hope it isn’t a lot of you.

“That selleth nations through her whoredoms.” She sells nations. They sold us; that is how we got over here. “And families through her witchcrafts.”

Meaning what? If you are down with America, you are down with the devil. That is what the Bible is telling us. Nahum saw the same thing John the Revelator saw: the judgment of the great harlot that sits upon many waters, and upon her forehead “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” An abomination is something the Lord hates and despises.

So her beauty is the beauty of a harlot and a witch that sold us. Desire her not for pleasure.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:4
precepts.why:
She says in her heart, “I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.” Some of y’all have taken on the characteristics of America, and it is time to shake that off. She is “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH”, and an abomination is what the Lord hates and despises. So it is time to come up out of her.

“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.”

That ye receive not of her plagues, because the Lord is still sending plagues. Y’all remember the pandemic. Stay with the Lord and come up out of her spiritually, so that her condemnation is not your condemnation.

That is what it means not to stumble at the beauty of the woman: don’t be mesmerized by her or desire her for pleasure, but come out of her, because her judgment is coming.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 28:7
precepts.why:
“Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations.” Contextually this is spoken to the king of Tyrus, who was said to be wiser than Daniel. But when you read the scriptures, a passage may speak contextually of one nation and prophetically of another, because the Lord shows “the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” Prophetically, this is Babylon the Great, America.

Who are the strangers, the terrible of the nations? The Allahu Akbar type strangers. Another word for it would be terrorists. “And they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom.” A lot of people thought America could never be touched. The Lord is showing you otherwise. When she begins to fall, she will be destroyed from the inside out, decaying, and then comes the great finale with the ten horns.

“And they shall defile thy brightness.” America likes to put on as if she is righteous, playing the moral world police, while she goes into countries, steals presidents and bombs everybody. That brightness will be defiled.

So don’t stumble at her beauty. The beauty of her wisdom and her brightness are exactly what the Lord has marked for the sword.

thread.label: Sirach 34:16
thread.text: For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon, a preservation from stumbling, and an help from falling.

precepts.label: Psalms 91:6
precepts.why:
“For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon”. God's eyes are on them that love him, and he is our mighty protection if we love him. A defence from what heat? Nuclear heat. And why a cover from the sun at noon? Because the destruction comes at noonday.

David shows it: “Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” The destruction wastes at noonday.

So all we have to do is be faithful and fear him, and he will protect us from the destruction to come. Sirach says the same of wisdom: “By her he shall be covered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.” By wisdom we shall be covered from the heat.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1-5
precepts.why:
The Lord is a defence from heat for them that love him, and in that day they will stand. “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” Why does he stand in boldness? Because he feared the Lord and stayed faithful.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear”. When the nations see it they will be troubled, saying, what the hell is this? They “shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” They cannot imagine it; they will not be able to fathom what is taking place when those chariots come.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach: We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints!”

The ones who mocked and afflicted the righteous will see him numbered among the children of God, protected while they are not.

precepts.label: Revelation 1:7
precepts.why:
The nations will be amazed at the strangeness of the salvation of the righteous, “so far beyond all that they looked for”, when those chariots come. John shows those chariots: “Behold, he cometh with clouds”. He is coming with clouds, and those clouds are his chariots.

And “every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.” Christ is returning with the multitude of angels, and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.

That is the day the Lord is “a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon” for them that love him: when every eye sees him coming, the righteous stand in boldness while the kindreds of the earth wail.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 3:16
precepts.why:
Christ is returning with clouds, with his chariots and the multitude of angels. Habakkuk saw it: “When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself”. Why did he tremble? Because Habakkuk was put in it. He felt it; he saw it.

He trembled “that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.” When Christ comes up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops, the angels.

That is the day of trouble in which the Lord is the mighty protection and strong stay of them that love him. The prophet trembled at what he saw, but those who fear the Lord will rest in that day.

precepts.label: Isaiah 31:4-5
precepts.why:
“For thus hath the Lord spoken unto me, Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey”. What is this talking about? The Lion of the tribe of Judah in Revelation 5:5: Christ.

And “when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof.” The Lord is going to fight for his people.

“As birds flying, so will the Lord of hosts defend Jerusalem”. As birds flying is Christ and the angels. And “defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it.” Passing over: this is the Passover season, and just as he passed over us in Egypt, he will pass over and preserve his people.

That is what it means that his eyes are upon them that love him and he is their mighty protection. He comes down as a roaring lion to fight for mount Zion and defend Jerusalem.

precepts.label: Revelation 5:5
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord will come down to fight for mount Zion “Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey”. Who is that lion? John shows it: “And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.”

That lion is Christ, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David. He is the one roaring on his prey, not afraid of the voice of the multitude of shepherds called against him, coming down with his angels as birds flying to defend Jerusalem. He is the mighty protection of them that love him.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 4:7
precepts.why:
The lion that roars on his prey is Christ, and Jeremiah shows him coming: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way”. This is twofold. It was talking about Nebuchadnezzar contextually, but prophetically it is talking about Jesus the Christ. He's coming.

And “he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.” He comes forth from his place to make the land of the Gentiles desolate, their cities laid waste without inhabitants.

So while the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way, the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, and he is their defence from the heat of that destruction.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 11:37
precepts.why:
The lion is Christ, roaring on his prey and coming up from his thicket as the destroyer of the Gentiles. Ezra saw the same lion: “And I beheld, and lo, as it were a roaring lion chased out of the wood: and I saw that he sent out a man’s voice unto the eagle”.

This eagle is America. The roaring lion sending his voice unto the eagle is Christ roaring against America, bringing destruction.

So when the destruction that wasteth at noonday comes on America, the Lord is the mighty protection of them that love him, a defence from heat and a cover from the sun at noon, while he roars against the eagle and fights for mount Zion.
